authority.source: Owner decision 2026-10-19: a bounded checked claim and an unbounded kernel-checked obligation; every definition is recovered from the withdrawal-queue contract.

scope: Every decision in the withdrawal-queue controller pilot: deposits, requests and ticks at now = 0; timeout withdrawals are outside this statement.

trace.event_schema: withdrawal-queue decision/1: pre-vault, command, context, outcome, post-vault and outbox
trace.order: authoritative commit order of the vault decisions, including rejections
trace.projection: retain every decision of the vault, accepted or rejected, without sorting, merging or deduplication
trace.model: the generated withdrawal-queue V2 contract evaluated by its checked Authority over the pilot domain: actions 160, 161 and 162, lanes 170 and 171, amounts 1 and 2, callers 190 through 193, either alarm value, and now fixed at 0; timeout withdrawals are excluded. The Lean model is its controller part (lanes, pause, must-serve, priority) under the actions tick, accepted request and other, checked row by row against the contract
trace.environment: any pilot command from any caller in any order: operator deposits, owner requests, keeper ticks with either alarm value, and rejected commands; now is fixed at 0, timeout withdrawals are excluded, and the alarm is taken as given
trace.initialization: the contract genesis (empty vault, both lanes empty, no pause, lane A first) commits and a changed genesis is refused; no request is pending at genesis, so a zero-operation execution holds no request
trace.transitions: every decision is an output of the checked Authority on a vault reachable from the genesis; each Lean model row equals the contract row it abstracts
trace.continuity: each post-vault is the next pre-vault; deposits and rejections leave the controller part unchanged, and an accepted request changes only its own empty lane, to arrived

assumptions.definition: A(sigma): the keeper's tick, which the contract accepts from every reachable vault, is taken infinitely often in sigma (weak fairness of exit processing). A assumes nothing about alarms, requests, deposits or other callers, and assumes neither completion nor alarm clearance. Delivery by the settlement rail is outside the contract.

A.definition: A(sigma): the keeper's tick, which the contract accepts from every reachable vault, is taken infinitely often in sigma (weak fairness of exit processing). A assumes nothing about alarms, requests, deposits or other callers, and assumes neither completion nor alarm clearance. Delivery by the settlement rail is outside the contract.

R.definition: the decision accepts the lane owner's RequestWithdrawal on lane r (rule 5, laws 501 and 502): the lane was empty and the amount is covered by the unreserved balance; a rejected request is no submission. A lane holds one request until its payout, so r names the request then occupying lane r, and the first lane-r payout after it is its own (checked).

C.definition: the decision is a keeper tick that pays lane r (rule 6, law 501): it queues one settlement payout of lane r with the amount that lane's request recorded, and empties the lane.

readings.body: forall sigma in Traces: A(sigma) => (forall r in Requests: always(R(r) => eventually(C(r))))
readings.intuitive: provided A, every legitimate submitted withdrawal eventually returns its matching assets, even when alarms occur
readings.plain: provided A, an alarm may delay a withdrawal but never freeze it
